reference.title: Dumbbell Gobelt Curtsey Lunge
reference.listing: Page could not be read (gymvisual.com blocked from this environment); movement taken from the exercise name and standard coaching
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

breathing.pattern: Inhale as you step back and lower, exhale as you drive back to standing.
breathing.cadence: About 1.8 s step and lower, short pause, about 1.5 s up and step in

prescription.tempo: Controlled step, 1-2 s down, about 1 s up
prescription.progression: Heavier dumbbells, a pause at the bottom, then a deficit (front foot on a low step). Dumbbell load is user-chosen: pick a weight that leaves about 2-3 reps in reserve (RPE 7-8) at the end of each set.

cues.text: Stand tall, feet hip width; hold one dumbbell upright against the chest, hands cupping the top plate, elbows down.
Step the right foot back and across, behind the left heel, landing on the ball of the foot; hips stay facing forward.
Breathe in and bend both knees; the front knee stays over the front foot, the dumbbell stays on the chest.
Breathe out, drive through the front heel and step the right foot back beside the left.
Stand tall and reset; alternate legs.

mistakes.fix: Keep the front knee over the second toe.

mistakes.mistake: Hips twisting toward the back leg
mistakes.fix: Keep both hip bones facing forward as you cross.
Keep it touching the sternum, elbows under it.

mistakes.mistake: Crossing so far that balance is lost
mistakes.fix: Land just past the front heel; cross less if you wobble.

kinematics.peak: Right ball of the foot 60 cm behind and 18 cm past the left ankle (crossing the midline)
kinematics.norm: Back foot lands behind and across the front foot (reference movement); no study gives a step length for the curtsy lunge (clinical opinion)
About 90 degrees at the bottom (clinical opinion)

kinematics.peak: ≈91°, 21.4 cm above the floor (knee joint centre)
kinematics.norm: Lowers behind the front heel without touching the floor (clinical opinion)
The back thigh crosses the midline (reference movement; clinical opinion)
Fairly upright; the load held at the chest helps keep the trunk tall (clinical opinion). Upright to slightly forward; trunk lean shifts work toward the hip extensors (Farrokhi 2008)

kinematics.setup: Upright at the sternum, hands cupping the top plate
kinematics.peak: Stays at the chest (≥2.63 cm from the body on the rig shapes)
kinematics.norm: Held upright at the sternum, elbows down (common coaching)

kinematics.peak: Step back 0.8 s, 1.0 s down, 0.3 s pause, 0.75 s up, step in 0.8 s
kinematics.norm: Controlled, about 1-2 s down and 1 s up (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #11686, Dumbbell Gobelt Curtsey Lunge, video (movement reference)
Hoogenboom, Ferguson, Krauss & Tran 2024, the reverse lunge: a descriptive electromyographic study (Applied Sciences 14(24):11480)
Hip-muscle activation during the lunge, single-leg squat, and step-up-and-over exercises (J Sport Rehabil 18(1):91-103, 2009; PubMed 19321909)
Farrokhi et al. 2008, trunk position influences lead-leg kinematics, kinetics and muscle activity in the forward lunge (J Orthop Sports Phys Ther 38:403-409)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness or giving-way occurs.
Choose a dumbbell load you can control for every rep; the load is user-chosen.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Clear the floor behind you before stepping back.
modify: Knee discomfort: cross less (land straight behind) and shorten the depth.
Balance concerns: practise the bodyweight version holding a support first.

muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Front (standing) leg hip extensor; in the reverse lunge gluteus maximus was more active in the stationary limb than in the stepping limb (Hoogenboom 2024).
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Front (standing) leg hip extensor; in the reverse lunge gluteus maximus was more active in the stationary limb than in the stepping limb (Hoogenboom 2024).
muscleNotes.quads_r: Front-leg knee extensors lower and raise the body; rectus femoris was more active in the stepping limb in the reverse lunge (Hoogenboom 2024).
muscleNotes.quads_l: Front-leg knee extensors lower and raise the body; rectus femoris was more active in the stepping limb in the reverse lunge (Hoogenboom 2024).
muscleNotes.glute_med_r: Front-leg hip abductor resists the knee caving in as the back leg crosses behind; in the reverse lunge only the stationary-limb gluteus medius reached a strengthening level (Hoogenboom 2024).
muscleNotes.glute_med_l: Front-leg hip abductor resists the knee caving in as the back leg crosses behind; in the reverse lunge only the stationary-limb gluteus medius reached a strengthening level (Hoogenboom 2024).
muscleNotes.adductors_r: Work on both legs to steady the crossed stance (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.adductors_l: Work on both legs to steady the crossed stance (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_r: Assist hip extension on the front leg (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_l: Assist hip extension on the front leg (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.calves_r: Steady the front shin; the back calf holds the heel up (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.calves_l: Steady the front shin; the back calf holds the heel up (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.core: Braces against the load held in front of the chest and keeps the pelvis level in the split stance (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.obliques_r: Resist the pelvis twisting toward the crossing leg (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.obliques_l: Resist the pelvis twisting toward the crossing leg (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_r: Cup the top plate and keep the dumbbell from slipping (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_l: Cup the top plate and keep the dumbbell from slipping (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.biceps_r: Hold the elbows bent and the dumbbell against the chest (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.biceps_l: Hold the elbows bent and the dumbbell against the chest (clinical opinion).
